stem.en: Kabir runs the day with only hormone B and the line crashes during cricket. He says "so hormone B is the dangerous one". What is the real lesson?

text.en: A single hormone can only push one way. Holding a line needs a push each way, proportional to the error. Insulin alone can lower and never raise; the sprint needed glucagon and adrenaline, which he did not have.

feedback.en: Too much of any one-way push is dangerous. Insulin at the right dose after a meal is exactly right.
Exercise is fine with both hormones working. The problem was one dial missing.

text.en: Hormone A should be on all day.

feedback.en: All-day glucagon empties the bank and sends the line high. Each hormone answers a specific error.

explanation.en: Two-sided control needs two pushes. Remove one side and the line can only drift the other way.
